name: The Message
artist: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five

podcast.body: Grandmaster Flash & The Furious Five's socially conscious 1982 single, an early rap classic that reached number 62. This song's elements were famously sampled by Sean Combs for Puff Daddy and Ma$e's 1997 number one hit "Can't Nobody Hold Me Down." "Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Fives socially conscious 1982 single The Message."

podcast.body: Released in 1982, this seminal track is noted as a significant advancement by the "great fathers of hip hop" during a period of rapid evolution where rap began to move away from its earlier boogie influences. "en 1982 gran master flasán de furios 5 se acaba de message."

srcs.episode: El RAP antes del RAP (los primeros años del rap)

podcast.body: This song marked a significant breakthrough for Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five in 1982. Its release further solidified the political and social commentary that would come to characterize much of hip hop in the mid to late 1980s, echoing the earlier thematic depth found in works like Gil Scott Heron's. "Sugar Hill then went on to sign Grandmaster Flash in the Furious Five who broke through in 1982 with the message."
